Not a photograph, not a photoreal render. Warm terracotta brick, faded teal wood, forest-green chalkboard, dusty rose and pale apricot sunlight. Premium detail comes from composition, painted depth and dramatic diagonal sunbeams. Modern Tamil college romance. No wedding-hotel decor, marble lobby, brass inlay, floral aisle, ribbon, phone, watermark or unrelated readable text.

A South Indian COLLEGE MAIN ACADEMIC BLOCK: weathered terracotta red-brick facade, cream lintels, shaded veranda, tall faded-teal timber double doors at the centre, each leaf with three rectangular solid panels and one simple dark iron handle. Three worn grey-granite entrance steps. Left of doors: a wooden campus noticeboard holding small blank pastel sheets. Right of doors: an old wooden student bench with two closed books. Timber classroom windows and leafy campus trees frame the building. Inside these doors is the ground-floor college lecture hall, not an event venue: honey-brown wooden student desks on both sides of ONE wide central aisle, tall barred classroom windows on LEFT, red-oxide floor, a large dark-green chalkboard mounted on the pale cream far wall. A simple wooden lectern stands off to the right of the chalkboard. No second set of doors. The two teal doors are completely CLOSED, hiding the classroom and chalkboard. Show enough brick facade, veranda, steps, noticeboard, student bench and overhead tree canopy that this is immediately recognisable as a college entrance. Doorway roughly central third of picture width; strong forward leading lines up the three steps. Apricot morning sky peeks above roof; diagonal sunshafts through rain-tree leaves. No humans or hands. NO visible text, not even on notices, books or lintel. Two small dry leaves levitate separately at the step edges, not a confetti storm.
